citations.chunk_id: 0045_Lu 等 - 2025 - All-climate carbonate electrolyte with 2-sulfobenzoic anhydride additive leads the way to high-perfo::sec7::child10
citations.quote: Under more extreme conditions, discharge tests at $-20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ (Fig. 4a) revealed that cells with SA-based electrolyte delivered discharge capacities of 758.6, 702.2 and $638.2\mathrm{mAh}$ at $0.2\mathrm{C}$ , $0.5\mathrm{C}$ , and $1\mathrm{C}$ ( $1\mathrm{C} = 900\mathrm{mA}$ ), respectively, outperforming those with the baseline electrolyte, which exhibited 706.3, 636.8 and $563.6\mathrm{mAh}$ . These results confirm that SA facilitates higher energy density and improved capacity retention at low temperatures, rendering it well-suited for emergency storage applications in cold environments. In addition, the rate capability of sodium-ion batteries at ambient temperature is critical for practical deployment. High-rate performance enables rapid charge/discharge cycles, a requirement for power-intensive applications such as electric vehicles and portable electronics [27a,28]. As shown in Fig. 4d, the SA containing system exhibited superior rate capacity, indicating enhanced commercial viability. Long-term cycling at 1C was also evaluated at room temperature (Figs. 4c and S7). During extended cycling, the baseline electrolyte showed faster polarization growth, whereas the SA-based system demonstrated superior capacity retention and enhanced coulombic efficiency. These characteristics contribute to reduced energy losses and extended battery lifespan, which are advantageous for grid-scale and commercial energy storage [29].

citations.quote:
In summary, we have successfully synthesized a multifunctional SA electrolyte additive for pouch NFM/HC sodium-ion batteries, enabling stable electrochemical performance across a wide operating temperature range ( $-20$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ ). The multifunctional role of the SA-containing electrolyte can be attributed to a combination of synergistic effects, including the regulation of $Na^{+}$ solvation structure to accelerate interfacial reaction kinetics and enhance electrochemical stability at low temperatures, the scavenging residual water to preserve the structural stability of the cathode and suppress excessive gas evolution, thereby enhancing high-temperature performance, and the preferential redox decomposition of SA on the anode surface to form a high-quality interfacial film that protects the electrode and reduces interfacial resistance. Collectively, this work provides new insights into the rational design and optimization of electrolyte additives for practical all-climate pouch SIBs and other advanced energy storage systems.

citations.chunk_id: 0002_Cai 等 - 2024 - A dual-functional electrolyte additive for stabilizing the solid electrolyte interphase and solvatio::sec2::child0
citations.quote: An electrolyte containing a sodium difluorophosphate (NaDFP) dual-functional additive is developed to enhance the temperature performance of $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). The addition of NaDFP in the electrolyte not only induces solid electrolyte interphases (SEIs) and cathode electrolyte interphases with excellent properties on the anode and cathode surfaces but also optimizes of the solvation structure of sodium ions, resulting in a better cycle stability of NFM/HC SIBs over a wide temperature range from $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . In addition, high capacity retentions of 85 % after 700 cycles at $25\ ^{\circ}C$ , 90 % after 150 cycles at $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ and 90 % after 150 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ are achieved, respectively. And those common problems such as gas generation and sodium evolution of pouch NFM/HC SIBs are also effectively relieved, indicating the promising application prospect of NaDFP additive in the functional electrolyte of NFM/HC SIBs.

citations.quote: Adopting the concept of using more comprehensive performance reflecting by pouch cells for experimental work, undoubtedly can make the researches have better academic and commercial value. Bases on the coupling of difluorophosphate-group with -tris(trimethylsilyl)-group in TDFP molecular, a difluorophosphate-based functional electrolyte is firstly developed to enhance the drastic temperature performance of pouch NFM/HC cells. This TDFP-containing electrolyte can realize a “formation-repair” film-formation aim and form tough and rich-NaF interfacial films on two electrodes. Different from NaDFP, TDFP can not only catalyze the decomposition of $PF_{6}^{-}$ to form NaF-rich SEI/CEI but also produce $PO_{2}F_{2}^{-}$ to optimize the film composition. Most importantly, it can pre-form a film on the electrode surface without charging, thus suppressing of solvent decomposition participation in film formation during charging. As results, the cycling and storage stability of pouch NFM/HC cells are considerably improved over a wide-temperature from $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ .

association_citations.quote: Adopting the concept of using more comprehensive performance reflecting by pouch cells for experimental work, undoubtedly can make the researches have better academic and commercial value. Bases on the coupling of difluorophosphate-group with -tris(trimethylsilyl)-group in TDFP molecular, a difluorophosphate-based functional electrolyte is firstly developed to enhance the drastic temperature performance of pouch NFM/HC cells. This TDFP-containing electrolyte can realize a “formation-repair” film-formation aim and form tough and rich-NaF interfacial films on two electrodes. Different from NaDFP, TDFP can not only catalyze the decomposition of $PF_{6}^{-}$ to form NaF-rich SEI/CEI but also produce $PO_{2}F_{2}^{-}$ to optimize the film composition. Most importantly, it can pre-form a film on the electrode surface without charging, thus suppressing of solvent decomposition participation in film formation during charging. As results, the cycling and storage stability of pouch NFM/HC cells are considerably improved over a wide-temperature from $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ .

citations.quote: The influence of incorporating various concentrations of NaTFPB on the NFM111 cathode was investigated through electrochemical measurements employing NFM111||Na half-cells. The rate capabilities of the half-cells with different electrolytes are depicted in Fig. 2a. Notably, the electrolyte containing 1.0 wt% NaTFPB exhibits superior rate performance, especially at high currents, due to its low interfacial resistance compared to the electrolytes with other concentrations. Even returned to 0.5 C, the discharged capacity of the electrolyte containing 1.0 wt% NaTFPB remains notably higher than that of the other electrolytes, recovering to 133.36 mAh g $^{-1}$ . Moreover, cyclic stability tests of the different electrolytes were conducted at a current density of 1.0 C (Fig. 2b). The results reveal that the 1.0 wt% NaTFPB electrolyte delivers a capacity retention of 70 % after 500 cycles at a current density of 1.0 C, significantly outperforming the Base electrolyte and other additive concentrations. Consequently, the concentration of NaTFPB additives was standardized to 1.0 wt%. Corresponding charge–discharge curves are presented in Fig. 2c-e. During the initial formation at a current density of 0.1 C, the electrolyte with 1.0 wt% NaTFPB delivered an ultra-high discharge specific capacity of 150.39 mAh g $^{-1}$ , compared to the capacity of 134.84 mAh g $^{-1}$ for the Base electrolyte (Fig. 2c).

citations.quote: Sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) are viable contenders for large-scale energy storage systems owing to the plentiful supply of sodium resources. However, the poor stability of electrolyte/ electrode interface severely limits the cycle life of SIBs. Herein, sodium tetrakis[3,5-bis(trifluoromethyl)phenyl]borate (NaTFPB), a boron-centered fluorinated organic sodium salt, is used as a bifunctional additive in the Base electrolyte (NaPF $_6$ in EC/DMC/FEC) for NaNi $_{0.33}$ Fe $_{0.33}$ Mn $_{0.33}$ O $_2$ |hard carbon pouch cells. Theoretical simulations and experimental studies demonstrate that NaTFPB modulates the first solvation shell structure of Na $^+$ and undergoes preferential redox reactions at both electrodes simultaneously. This behaviour contributes to the formation of robust interfacial layers. As a result, uniform and stable cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI) and solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) layers, enriched with NaF and boron compounds, are formed. The Ah-scale pouch cell with NaTFPB exhibits a high capacity retention of 79 % after 500 cycles at 1 C rate under room temperature. Remarkably, under harsh operational stress combining elevated temperature (45 °C) and an upper high cutoff voltage of 4.1 V, the cell retains 96 % capacity retention over 250 cycles. Additionally, it exhibits excellent low-temperature discharge capability at $-20$ °C.

citations.quote: The NFM111||HC pouch cells (1.4 Ah) are assembled to validate the significant potential of the additive in practical applications. Fig. 7a visually presents the cycling performance of the NFM111||HC pouch cell within the voltage range of 2.0–3.95 V at 25 °C. The cell containing the NaTFPB additive maintains a high capacity retention of 79 % after 500 cycles at a current density of 1.0 C, whereas the cell with the Base electrolyte retains only 62 % of its capacity. The rapid capacity degradation of the Base electrolyte cell is attributed to the poor stability of CEI/SEI and continuous decomposition of the electrolyte. The digital photographs of cycled electrodes reveal that the Base system exhibits yellow and white decomposition products while the electrodes with NaTFPB appear clean (Fig. S19). The charge–discharge curves in Fig. 7b-c display the initial discharge capacity of the NaTFPB electrolyte system reaching 1.35 Ah during the first cycle, significantly outperforming the Base electrolyte system's 1.27 Ah. After 500 cycles, the discharge capacity of the Base electrolyte system drops to 0.79 Ah, while the NaTFPB system still maintains an impressive capacity of 1.07 Ah. It is worth emphasizing that the pouch cell with the NaTFPB electrolyte system exhibits significant advantages in cycling performance compared to those of the previous research findings (Fig. S20).

TMSB or TMSP were respectively added into the baseline electrolyte and assigned as NB or NP electrolyte. All electrolytes were prepared in a dry argon filled glove box with both moisture and oxygen concentrations below 0.1 ppm. NFM was purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co, Ltd, HC was purchased from Kuraray Co Ltd. The pouch test cells with NFM cathode (120 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.1 C), HC anode (290 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.05 C), and Celgard 2700 separator were assembled using the conventional assembly method. Therein, NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotube (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and Maleic acid (the reason of addition maleic acid was shown in Table 1) were dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) with a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate to prepare the NFM cathode.

citations.chunk_id: 0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec2
citations.quote:
ABSTRACT
A “hard-soft synergy” strategy is firstly developed to design functional multi-component electrolytes and successfully achieve drastic temperature performance of $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) over a wide range from $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . Coupling “hard”-sodium difluorophosphate (NaDFP) with “soft”-tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphate (TMSP) or tris(trimethylsilyl) borate (TMSB) reasonably realizes an optimized solvation structure from “solvent dominated” to “anion collaborative” and synergistic-formed tough and multi-component interfacial films. Benefit to these, the cycling stability is considerably improved under the room and cold conditions, the capacity retention after 350 cycles increases from 0 % to 92 % and even stable cycling performance at 1 C (1 C = 900 mA) can be obtained at $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ . Discharge capacity at $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ and the capacity retention after storage at $60\ ^{\circ}C$ are also greatly improved. Furthermore, the functional mechanisms of different electrolyte combinations under extreme temperature conditions are analyzed. It is demonstrated that the combination of NaDFP and TMSP is more suitable for high-temperature requirements due to its tougher cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI), reduced transition metal dissolution, and minimized cathode phase deviation. In contrast, the combination of NaDFP and TMSB is more suitable for low-temperature requirements, benefiting from the reduced desolvation energy and viscosity. In addition to the obtained functional electrolytes, this work also provides new insight for designing functional multi-component electrolytes of SIBs.

These results confirm that SA facilitates higher energy density and improved capacity retention at low temperatures, rendering it well-suited for emergency storage applications in cold environments. In addition, the rate capability of sodium-ion batteries at ambient temperature is critical for practical deployment. High-rate performance enables rapid charge/discharge cycles, a requirement for power-intensive applications such as electric vehicles and portable electronics [27a,28]. As shown in Fig. 4d, the SA containing system exhibited superior rate capacity, indicating enhanced commercial viability. Long-term cycling at 1C was also evaluated at room temperature (Figs. 4c and S7). During extended cycling, the baseline electrolyte showed faster polarization growth, whereas the SA-based system demonstrated superior capacity retention and enhanced coulombic efficiency. evidence_ledger.quote: Sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) are viable contenders for large-scale energy storage systems owing to the plentiful supply of sodium resources. However, the poor stability of electrolyte/ electrode interface severely limits the cycle life of SIBs. Herein, sodium tetrakis[3,5-bis(trifluoromethyl)phenyl]borate (NaTFPB), a boron-centered fluorinated organic sodium salt, is used as a bifunctional additive in the Base electrolyte (NaPF $_6$ in EC/DMC/FEC) for NaNi $_{0.33}$ Fe $_{0.33}$ Mn $_{0.33}$ O $_2$ |hard carbon pouch cells. Theoretical simulations and experimental studies demonstrate that NaTFPB modulates the first solvation shell structure of Na $^+$ and undergoes preferential redox reactions at both electrodes simultaneously. This behaviour contributes to the formation of robust interfacial layers. As a result, uniform and stable cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI) and solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) layers, enriched with NaF and boron compounds, are formed. The Ah-scale pouch cell with NaTFPB exhibits a high capacity retention of 79 % after 500 cycles at 1 C rate under room temperature. Remarkably, under harsh operational stress combining elevated temperature (45 °C) and an upper high cutoff voltage of 4.1 V, the cell retains 96 % capacity retention over 250 cycles. Additionally, it exhibits excellent low-temperature discharge capability at $-20$ °C.

evidence_ledger.chunk_id: 0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec2
evidence_ledger.paper_id: 0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o
evidence_ledger.quote:
ABSTRACT
A “hard-soft synergy” strategy is firstly developed to design functional multi-component electrolytes and successfully achieve drastic temperature performance of $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) over a wide range from $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . Coupling “hard”-sodium difluorophosphate (NaDFP) with “soft”-tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphate (TMSP) or tris(trimethylsilyl) borate (TMSB) reasonably realizes an optimized solvation structure from “solvent dominated” to “anion collaborative” and synergistic-formed tough and multi-component interfacial films. Benefit to these, the cycling stability is considerably improved under the room and cold conditions, the capacity retention after 350 cycles increases from 0 % to 92 % and even stable cycling performance at 1 C (1 C = 900 mA) can be obtained at $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ . Discharge capacity at $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ and the capacity retention after storage at $60\ ^{\circ}C$ are also greatly improved. Furthermore, the functional mechanisms of different electrolyte combinations under extreme temperature conditions are analyzed. It is demonstrated that the combination of NaDFP and TMSP is more suitable for high-temperature requirements due to its tougher cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI), reduced transition metal dissolution, and minimized cathode phase deviation. In contrast, the combination of NaDFP and TMSB is more suitable for low-temperature requirements, benefiting from the reduced desolvation energy and viscosity. In addition to the obtained functional electrolytes, this work also provides new insight for designing functional multi-component electrolytes of SIBs.

citations.quote: A multifunctional additive, 2-sulfobenzoic anhydride (SA), was synthesized from the readily available saccharin, then 1 % SA was added into carbonate-based electrolytes to enhance the performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) employing $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM) cathodes and hard carbon (HC) anodes across a wide temperature range from $-20\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . The commercial pouch cells delivered a capacity retention of 90.52 % after 300 cycles at room temperature and 92.28 % after 300 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ . Low-temperature rate performance at $-20\ ^{\circ}C$ and cycling at $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ further demonstrated the excellent adaptability of SA-containing electrolytes under sub-zero temperature. Moreover, under high-voltage operation at 4.0 V, the SA-containing electrolyte effectively suppressed capacity fading, resulting in an 11.44 % improvement in capacity retention. Compared to conventional commercial electrolytes, this electrolyte enables interfacial optimization by suppressing excessive growth of cathode and anode interphases, also it eliminates detrimental electrolyte components, tune the solvation structure and promote interfacial reaction kinetics. In situ gas analysis conducted during cycling at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ revealed that SA significantly inhibits gas-evolving side reactions, thereby ensuring the safety of SIBs.

In summary, we have successfully synthesized a multifunctional SA electrolyte additive for pouch NFM/HC sodium-ion batteries, enabling stable electrochemical performance across a wide operating temperature range ( $-20$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ ). The multifunctional role of the SA-containing electrolyte can be attributed to a combination of synergistic effects, including the regulation of $Na^{+}$ solvation structure to accelerate interfacial reaction kinetics and enhance electrochemical stability at low temperatures, the scavenging residual water to preserve the structural stability of the cathode and suppress excessive gas evolution, thereby enhancing high-temperature performance, and the preferential redox decomposition of SA on the anode surface to form a high-quality interfacial film that protects the electrode and reduces interfacial resistance. Collectively, this work provides new insights into the rational design and optimization of electrolyte additives for practical all-climate pouch SIBs and other advanced energy storage systems.

citations.quote: An electrolyte containing a sodium difluorophosphate (NaDFP) dual-functional additive is developed to enhance the temperature performance of $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). The addition of NaDFP in the electrolyte not only induces solid electrolyte interphases (SEIs) and cathode electrolyte interphases with excellent properties on the anode and cathode surfaces but also optimizes of the solvation structure of sodium ions, resulting in a better cycle stability of NFM/HC SIBs over a wide temperature range from $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . In addition, high capacity retentions of 85 % after 700 cycles at $25\ ^{\circ}C$ , 90 % after 150 cycles at $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ and 90 % after 150 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ are achieved, respectively. And those common problems such as gas generation and sodium evolution of pouch NFM/HC SIBs are also effectively relieved, indicating the promising application prospect of NaDFP additive in the functional electrolyte of NFM/HC SIBs.

citations.quote: Adopting the concept of using more comprehensive performance reflecting by pouch cells for experimental work, undoubtedly can make the researches have better academic and commercial value. Bases on the coupling of difluorophosphate-group with -tris(trimethylsilyl)-group in TDFP molecular, a difluorophosphate-based functional electrolyte is firstly developed to enhance the drastic temperature performance of pouch NFM/HC cells. This TDFP-containing electrolyte can realize a “formation-repair” film-formation aim and form tough and rich-NaF interfacial films on two electrodes. Different from NaDFP, TDFP can not only catalyze the decomposition of $PF_{6}^{-}$ to form NaF-rich SEI/CEI but also produce $PO_{2}F_{2}^{-}$ to optimize the film composition. Most importantly, it can pre-form a film on the electrode surface without charging, thus suppressing of solvent decomposition participation in film formation during charging. As results, the cycling and storage stability of pouch NFM/HC cells are considerably improved over a wide-temperature from $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ .

The rate capabilities of the half-cells with different electrolytes are depicted in Fig. 2a. Notably, the electrolyte containing 1.0 wt% NaTFPB exhibits superior rate performance, especially at high currents, due to its low interfacial resistance compared to the electrolytes with other concentrations. citations.quote: Sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) are viable contenders for large-scale energy storage systems owing to the plentiful supply of sodium resources. However, the poor stability of electrolyte/ electrode interface severely limits the cycle life of SIBs. Herein, sodium tetrakis[3,5-bis(trifluoromethyl)phenyl]borate (NaTFPB), a boron-centered fluorinated organic sodium salt, is used as a bifunctional additive in the Base electrolyte (NaPF $_6$ in EC/DMC/FEC) for NaNi $_{0.33}$ Fe $_{0.33}$ Mn $_{0.33}$ O $_2$ |hard carbon pouch cells. Theoretical simulations and experimental studies demonstrate that NaTFPB modulates the first solvation shell structure of Na $^+$ and undergoes preferential redox reactions at both electrodes simultaneously. This behaviour contributes to the formation of robust interfacial layers. As a result, uniform and stable cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI) and solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) layers, enriched with NaF and boron compounds, are formed. The Ah-scale pouch cell with NaTFPB exhibits a high capacity retention of 79 % after 500 cycles at 1 C rate under room temperature. Remarkably, under harsh operational stress combining elevated temperature (45 °C) and an upper high cutoff voltage of 4.1 V, the cell retains 96 % capacity retention over 250 cycles. Additionally, it exhibits excellent low-temperature discharge capability at $-20$ °C.

citations.quote: The NFM111||HC pouch cells (1.4 Ah) are assembled to validate the significant potential of the additive in practical applications. Fig. 7a visually presents the cycling performance of the NFM111||HC pouch cell within the voltage range of 2.0–3.95 V at 25 °C. The cell containing the NaTFPB additive maintains a high capacity retention of 79 % after 500 cycles at a current density of 1.0 C, whereas the cell with the Base electrolyte retains only 62 % of its capacity. The rapid capacity degradation of the Base electrolyte cell is attributed to the poor stability of CEI/SEI and continuous decomposition of the electrolyte. The digital photographs of cycled electrodes reveal that the Base system exhibits yellow and white decomposition products while the electrodes with NaTFPB appear clean (Fig. S19). The charge–discharge curves in Fig. 7b-c display the initial discharge capacity of the NaTFPB electrolyte system reaching 1.35 Ah during the first cycle, significantly outperforming the Base electrolyte system's 1.27 Ah. After 500 cycles, the discharge capacity of the Base electrolyte system drops to 0.79 Ah, while the NaTFPB system still maintains an impressive capacity of 1.07 Ah. It is worth emphasizing that the pouch cell with the NaTFPB electrolyte system exhibits significant advantages in cycling performance compared to those of the previous research findings (Fig. S20).

citations.quote: It is worth emphasizing that the pouch cell with the NaTFPB electrolyte system exhibits significant advantages in cycling performance compared to those of the previous research findings (Fig. S20). Moreover, the NaTFPB additive also significantly enhances the cycling stability of pouch cells under high temperature and high voltage conditions (Fig. 7d). Under harsh conditions of 4.1 V and 45 °C, the pouch cell with Base electrolyte experienced a sharp capacity retention drop to 80 % after only 112 cycles (Fig. S21). This is attributed to the continuous decomposition of organic solvents, leading to severe gas generation within the pouch cell. In contrast, the NaTFPB additive stabilizes the interface by forming robust SEI/CEI layers enriched with NaF and boron compounds, significantly suppressing gas generation (Fig. S22). As a result, the pouch cell with NaTFPB maintained an exceptional capacity retention of 96 % after 250 cycles. The parallel sample error analysis in Fig. S23 further confirms the superior consistency and stability of the NaTFPB system, with smaller deviations in both initial capacity and capacity retention rate compared to the Base electrolyte, highlighting its reliability for practical applications. When the working temperature decreases to -20 °C, the pouch cell with NaTFBP additive displays discharge capacities of 1.07 Ah at 0.5 C under a high voltage of 4.1 V (Fig. 7e), much higher than that with the Base electrolyte (1.01 Ah).

citations.chunk_id: 0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec2
citations.quote:
ABSTRACT
A “hard-soft synergy” strategy is firstly developed to design functional multi-component electrolytes and successfully achieve drastic temperature performance of $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) over a wide range from $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . Coupling “hard”-sodium difluorophosphate (NaDFP) with “soft”-tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphate (TMSP) or tris(trimethylsilyl) borate (TMSB) reasonably realizes an optimized solvation structure from “solvent dominated” to “anion collaborative” and synergistic-formed tough and multi-component interfacial films. Benefit to these, the cycling stability is considerably improved under the room and cold conditions, the capacity retention after 350 cycles increases from 0 % to 92 % and even stable cycling performance at 1 C (1 C = 900 mA) can be obtained at $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ . Discharge capacity at $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ and the capacity retention after storage at $60\ ^{\circ}C$ are also greatly improved. Furthermore, the functional mechanisms of different electrolyte combinations under extreme temperature conditions are analyzed. It is demonstrated that the combination of NaDFP and TMSP is more suitable for high-temperature requirements due to its tougher cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI), reduced transition metal dissolution, and minimized cathode phase deviation. In contrast, the combination of NaDFP and TMSB is more suitable for low-temperature requirements, benefiting from the reduced desolvation energy and viscosity. In addition to the obtained functional electrolytes, this work also provides new insight for designing functional multi-component electrolytes of SIBs.

citations.quote: A multifunctional additive, 2-sulfobenzoic anhydride (SA), was synthesized from the readily available saccharin, then 1 % SA was added into carbonate-based electrolytes to enhance the performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) employing $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM) cathodes and hard carbon (HC) anodes across a wide temperature range from $-20\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . The commercial pouch cells delivered a capacity retention of 90.52 % after 300 cycles at room temperature and 92.28 % after 300 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ . Low-temperature rate performance at $-20\ ^{\circ}C$ and cycling at $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ further demonstrated the excellent adaptability of SA-containing electrolytes under sub-zero temperature. Moreover, under high-voltage operation at 4.0 V, the SA-containing electrolyte effectively suppressed capacity fading, resulting in an 11.44 % improvement in capacity retention. Compared to conventional commercial electrolytes, this electrolyte enables interfacial optimization by suppressing excessive growth of cathode and anode interphases, also it eliminates detrimental electrolyte components, tune the solvation structure and promote interfacial reaction kinetics. In situ gas analysis conducted during cycling at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ revealed that SA significantly inhibits gas-evolving side reactions, thereby ensuring the safety of SIBs.

In summary, we have successfully synthesized a multifunctional SA electrolyte additive for pouch NFM/HC sodium-ion batteries, enabling stable electrochemical performance across a wide operating temperature range ( $-20$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ ). The multifunctional role of the SA-containing electrolyte can be attributed to a combination of synergistic effects, including the regulation of $Na^{+}$ solvation structure to accelerate interfacial reaction kinetics and enhance electrochemical stability at low temperatures, the scavenging residual water to preserve the structural stability of the cathode and suppress excessive gas evolution, thereby enhancing high-temperature performance, and the preferential redox decomposition of SA on the anode surface to form a high-quality interfacial film that protects the electrode and reduces interfacial resistance. Collectively, this work provides new insights into the rational design and optimization of electrolyte additives for practical all-climate pouch SIBs and other advanced energy storage systems.

citations.chunk_id: 0002_Cai 等 - 2024 - A dual-functional electrolyte additive for stabilizing the solid electrolyte interphase and solvatio::sec2::child0
citations.quote: An electrolyte containing a sodium difluorophosphate (NaDFP) dual-functional additive is developed to enhance the temperature performance of $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). The addition of NaDFP in the electrolyte not only induces solid electrolyte interphases (SEIs) and cathode electrolyte interphases with excellent properties on the anode and cathode surfaces but also optimizes of the solvation structure of sodium ions, resulting in a better cycle stability of NFM/HC SIBs over a wide temperature range from $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . In addition, high capacity retentions of 85 % after 700 cycles at $25\ ^{\circ}C$ , 90 % after 150 cycles at $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ and 90 % after 150 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ are achieved, respectively. And those common problems such as gas generation and sodium evolution of pouch NFM/HC SIBs are also effectively relieved, indicating the promising application prospect of NaDFP additive in the functional electrolyte of NFM/HC SIBs.

citations.quote: Adopting the concept of using more comprehensive performance reflecting by pouch cells for experimental work, undoubtedly can make the researches have better academic and commercial value. Bases on the coupling of difluorophosphate-group with -tris(trimethylsilyl)-group in TDFP molecular, a difluorophosphate-based functional electrolyte is firstly developed to enhance the drastic temperature performance of pouch NFM/HC cells. This TDFP-containing electrolyte can realize a “formation-repair” film-formation aim and form tough and rich-NaF interfacial films on two electrodes. Different from NaDFP, TDFP can not only catalyze the decomposition of $PF_{6}^{-}$ to form NaF-rich SEI/CEI but also produce $PO_{2}F_{2}^{-}$ to optimize the film composition. Most importantly, it can pre-form a film on the electrode surface without charging, thus suppressing of solvent decomposition participation in film formation during charging. As results, the cycling and storage stability of pouch NFM/HC cells are considerably improved over a wide-temperature from $-40\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ .

citations.quote: This is likely attributable to the sharp decline in conductivity and the surge in viscosity caused by NaDFP at low temperatures, which weakened the electrolyte's kinetic performance and resulted in inferior rate performance compared to cells with TMSP and TDFP. Furthermore, performance tests were conducted at even lower temperatures, and it was found that the cells with TDFP still maintained an 86% discharge capacity retention rate at -30 °C. Low temperature cycling test is followed to further validate the superior performance of TDFP. As illustrated in Fig. 4d, the cell with TDFP exhibited the best cycling stability, followed by TMSP, then NaDFP, and finally the Baseline. It is worth noting that the performance of TMSP and NaDFP batteries under low-temperature cycling was the reverse of that under room-temperature cycling. This suggests that the failure mechanisms of the batteries and the reasons for performance enhancement by additives also differ. The thicknesses of cells haven't visible change before and after cycling, meaning no significant gas generation could be observed under low-temperature conditions (Fig. 4e). This contrasts with the results under room-temperature cycling, leading to the slightly better performance of TMSP-containing cells compared to NaDFP-containing cells under low-temperature conditions.

The rate capabilities of the half-cells with different electrolytes are depicted in Fig. 2a. Notably, the electrolyte containing 1.0 wt% NaTFPB exhibits superior rate performance, especially at high currents, due to its low interfacial resistance compared to the electrolytes with other concentrations. citations.chunk_id: 0024_Hu 等 - 2025 - Bifunctional sodium tetrakis 35-bistrifluoromethylphenyl borate additive for long-lifespan sodi::sec3::child0
citations.quote: Sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) are viable contenders for large-scale energy storage systems owing to the plentiful supply of sodium resources. However, the poor stability of electrolyte/ electrode interface severely limits the cycle life of SIBs. Herein, sodium tetrakis[3,5-bis(trifluoromethyl)phenyl]borate (NaTFPB), a boron-centered fluorinated organic sodium salt, is used as a bifunctional additive in the Base electrolyte (NaPF $_6$ in EC/DMC/FEC) for NaNi $_{0.33}$ Fe $_{0.33}$ Mn $_{0.33}$ O $_2$ |hard carbon pouch cells. Theoretical simulations and experimental studies demonstrate that NaTFPB modulates the first solvation shell structure of Na $^+$ and undergoes preferential redox reactions at both electrodes simultaneously. This behaviour contributes to the formation of robust interfacial layers. As a result, uniform and stable cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI) and solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) layers, enriched with NaF and boron compounds, are formed. The Ah-scale pouch cell with NaTFPB exhibits a high capacity retention of 79 % after 500 cycles at 1 C rate under room temperature. Remarkably, under harsh operational stress combining elevated temperature (45 °C) and an upper high cutoff voltage of 4.1 V, the cell retains 96 % capacity retention over 250 cycles. Additionally, it exhibits excellent low-temperature discharge capability at $-20$ °C.

citations.quote: The NFM111||HC pouch cells (1.4 Ah) are assembled to validate the significant potential of the additive in practical applications. Fig. 7a visually presents the cycling performance of the NFM111||HC pouch cell within the voltage range of 2.0–3.95 V at 25 °C. The cell containing the NaTFPB additive maintains a high capacity retention of 79 % after 500 cycles at a current density of 1.0 C, whereas the cell with the Base electrolyte retains only 62 % of its capacity. The rapid capacity degradation of the Base electrolyte cell is attributed to the poor stability of CEI/SEI and continuous decomposition of the electrolyte. The digital photographs of cycled electrodes reveal that the Base system exhibits yellow and white decomposition products while the electrodes with NaTFPB appear clean (Fig. S19). The charge–discharge curves in Fig. 7b-c display the initial discharge capacity of the NaTFPB electrolyte system reaching 1.35 Ah during the first cycle, significantly outperforming the Base electrolyte system's 1.27 Ah. After 500 cycles, the discharge capacity of the Base electrolyte system drops to 0.79 Ah, while the NaTFPB system still maintains an impressive capacity of 1.07 Ah. It is worth emphasizing that the pouch cell with the NaTFPB electrolyte system exhibits significant advantages in cycling performance compared to those of the previous research findings (Fig. S20).

citations.quote: It is worth emphasizing that the pouch cell with the NaTFPB electrolyte system exhibits significant advantages in cycling performance compared to those of the previous research findings (Fig. S20). Moreover, the NaTFPB additive also significantly enhances the cycling stability of pouch cells under high temperature and high voltage conditions (Fig. 7d). Under harsh conditions of 4.1 V and 45 °C, the pouch cell with Base electrolyte experienced a sharp capacity retention drop to 80 % after only 112 cycles (Fig. S21). This is attributed to the continuous decomposition of organic solvents, leading to severe gas generation within the pouch cell. In contrast, the NaTFPB additive stabilizes the interface by forming robust SEI/CEI layers enriched with NaF and boron compounds, significantly suppressing gas generation (Fig. S22). As a result, the pouch cell with NaTFPB maintained an exceptional capacity retention of 96 % after 250 cycles. The parallel sample error analysis in Fig. S23 further confirms the superior consistency and stability of the NaTFPB system, with smaller deviations in both initial capacity and capacity retention rate compared to the Base electrolyte, highlighting its reliability for practical applications. When the working temperature decreases to -20 °C, the pouch cell with NaTFBP additive displays discharge capacities of 1.07 Ah at 0.5 C under a high voltage of 4.1 V (Fig. 7e), much higher than that with the Base electrolyte (1.01 Ah).

Fig. 7a visually presents the cycling performance of the NFM111||HC pouch cell within the voltage range of 2.0–3.95 V at 25 °C. The cell containing the NaTFPB additive maintains a high capacity retention of 79 % after 500 cycles at a current density of 1.0 C, whereas the cell with the Base electrolyte retains only 62 % of its capacity. The rapid capacity degradation of the Base electrolyte cell is attributed to the poor stability of CEI/SEI and continuous decomposition of the electrolyte. The charge–discharge curves in Fig. 7b-c display the initial discharge capacity of the NaTFPB electrolyte system reaching 1.35 Ah during the first cycle, significantly outperforming the Base electrolyte system's 1.27 Ah. After 500 cycles, the discharge capacity of the Base electrolyte system drops to 0.79 Ah, while the NaTFPB system still maintains an impressive capacity of 1.07 Ah. It is worth emphasizing that the pouch cell with the NaTFPB electrolyte system exhibits significant advantages in cycling performance compared to those of the previous research findings (Fig. S20).

When the working temperature decreases to -20 °C, the pouch cell with NaTFBP additive displays discharge capacities of 1.07 Ah at 0.5 C under a high voltage of 4.1 V (Fig. 7e), much higher than that with the Base electrolyte (1.01 Ah).

citations.chunk_id: 0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec2
citations.quote:
ABSTRACT
A “hard-soft synergy” strategy is firstly developed to design functional multi-component electrolytes and successfully achieve drastic temperature performance of $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) over a wide range from $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . Coupling “hard”-sodium difluorophosphate (NaDFP) with “soft”-tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphate (TMSP) or tris(trimethylsilyl) borate (TMSB) reasonably realizes an optimized solvation structure from “solvent dominated” to “anion collaborative” and synergistic-formed tough and multi-component interfacial films. Benefit to these, the cycling stability is considerably improved under the room and cold conditions, the capacity retention after 350 cycles increases from 0 % to 92 % and even stable cycling performance at 1 C (1 C = 900 mA) can be obtained at $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ . Discharge capacity at $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ and the capacity retention after storage at $60\ ^{\circ}C$ are also greatly improved. Furthermore, the functional mechanisms of different electrolyte combinations under extreme temperature conditions are analyzed. It is demonstrated that the combination of NaDFP and TMSP is more suitable for high-temperature requirements due to its tougher cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI), reduced transition metal dissolution, and minimized cathode phase deviation. In contrast, the combination of NaDFP and TMSB is more suitable for low-temperature requirements, benefiting from the reduced desolvation energy and viscosity. In addition to the obtained functional electrolytes, this work also provides new insight for designing functional multi-component electrolytes of SIBs.

Furthermore, to evaluate dual additive potential at tougher low-temperatures, $-20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and $-30^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ discharge tests are necessary. Fig. 4e shows the capacity retention of pouch cells at different discharge currents, revealing the cells all can exhibit good electrochemical performance under the tested temperature conditions. Even at $-30^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and $1\mathrm{C}$ , the discharge capacity of pouch cells with NP and NB electrolytes still achieves $729\mathrm{mAh}$ and $697\mathrm{mAh}$ , respectively. These results confirm that this co-additive addition strategy improves extremely low temperature performance of NFM/HC pouch cells. Summarily, compared to single additive or baseline electrolyte, NFM/HC pouch cells with multi-component functional electrolyte possess much better performance. Therein, the cells containing NP electrolyte have better room and high-temperature performance, and the cells containing NB electrolyte are more suitable for low-temperature application.

## 任务要求与测试类型

整理配方前，先检查候选是否报告了用户要求的温度、倍率和电池配置下的结果。
标题相关或正文分别出现这些条件，不代表同一次试验满足全部条件。
先补取与目标工况相符的性能段，再整理对应配方的浓度、比例和添加剂用量。
若已选候选缺少目标条件下的结果，应检查本轮检索返回的其他候选，
不要围绕同一候选重复查询，或把另一温度下的表现当作目标条件的结果。

先把用户明确要求的条件写入 `constraint_records`，不要在筛选过程中增加用户没有
提出的性能要求。放电容量、倍率性能和循环寿命是不同测试。用户要求某温度、某倍率
的放电结果时，不将缺少同温度、同倍率的循环寿命结果记为阻断缺口。
`unresolved_gaps` 应对应候选组成缺失或用户必需条件，额外研究建议写进验证计划。
若原文已经明写倍率与电流的对应关系，应引用该原句，不将它再次列为缺失。
用户给出的数值与单位须原样保留在至少一个检索查询中，包括括号内的电流或容量。
不能用倍率替换具体电流后就认为已经检索了全部条件。具体标识未命中时先核查
原标识的字面检索结果，再继续扩展候选；不由系统填写论文名称或配方。
在形成候选前，逐项检查用户目标是否已有相关证据。近似温度是选材目标，仍需
优先考察接近该目标的实际测试结果；室温表现不能替代高温或低温使用依据。
近似目标没有容差时不虚构数值阈值。报告必须写出文献实测条件，并在 next_steps
交代目标条件下的验证；不能省略这个目标后把基础配方写成完整解决方案。
成本等定性目标也逐项说明已有依据和待验证事项，不能随硬条件通过而消失。
联合条件的 `electrode` 只写正负极材料，`cell_configuration` 单独写软包、扣式等
电池类型，不把两种信息混写在一个字段中。

- 用户要求设计适用于特定工况（低温、高压、长循环等）的钠离子电池电解液；
- 用户提供多套候选配方要求评分筛选。

## 工作流

### 逆向设计例外：先诊断，筛选仅决定能否推荐配方

对于容量骤降、首圈库仑效率低、高压衰减、阻抗增长等 `inverse_design` 问题，先从检索证据中建立至少两个可区分的电解液侧假设，并提出能区分它们的 EIS、Raman、XPS、LSV、ICP、产气或对照实验。仍执行候选配方筛选，但筛选 `hold` 只禁止“推荐进入实验”的完整配方；不得因此省略诊断、混杂因素和条件化调整方向。报告必须区分“已被证据支持的诊断事实”与“待验证的调整方向”。

1. 解析用户目标与约束；把用户要求的每项条件写成结构化 `constraint_records`，例如：
   不得把整段用户问题放入 `target_conditions`，再把旧文本检查识别到的部分词语当成全部要求。
   推荐前逐项核对用户要求与检查条件，避免漏掉正极、负极、电池形式、温度、倍率或指标定义。
   检索前先解释用户给出的数值条件：它描述什么物理量、单位如何理解、哪些信息尚不明确。
   这一解释依据用户描述的工作场景，在检索前定下，不能由后来检索到的论文或知识图谱记录
   反过来改写；其它论文里恰好出现同样的 “N C” 写法，只说明那些论文的用法，不能用来判断
   用户这句话。
   温度与倍率的单位必须分清。省略度符号的 C 不能直接视为充放电倍率。
   按它在句中的位置判断：直接修饰电芯、电池或其使用环境时（如 “a pouch cell at -30 C”、
   “a full cell around 50 C”），是温度；只有与充放电动作或倍率词连用时
   （如 “discharged at 1 C”、“cycled at 0.5 C”、“1 C rate”），才是倍率。
   按上下文确定一种解释后，就用这一种建立约束，
   不因缺少度符号再补一条互斥的倍率或温度约束，也不因检索结果改回另一种解释。
   检索查询和筛选断言须明确写出所采用的
   物理量与单位。只有上下文确实无法确定物理量时，才同时列出两种解释并说明需要澄清，
   此时暂缓推荐，而不是把两种解释同时写成两条互斥的数值约束。
   接近目标温度的文献结果应保留实测温度，不能改写为目标温度。
   硬约束来自用户问题，不得自行加上某一正极、软包形式、长循环寿命或数值阈值。
   在若干可替代选项之间尚未确定时（例如某类溶剂或某类盐有多种候选），不得把它们
   同时写成必需的 `required_component`；每个选项应作为独立候选分别比较，不叠加互斥的必需组分。
   近似目标也必须进入筛选，不得因用户没有给出容差而省略。保留用户对目标的原话，
   用现有 `evidence_claim` 表达候选须有相应工况下的直接测试依据，而非把近似目标
   改成精确相等、单边不等式或自行设定容差。逐候选判断时，`supported` 须引用该
   候选的实际测试条件与性能原句，`basis` 写清实测条件与目标的差别及其关联依据。
   只有其他工况的结果、测试建议或机理预测时，不能据此判近似工况要求已满足。
   没有相应测试依据就保留 `not_found` 并补证，不能删掉该要求后批准推荐，再把它

   联合条件也须保留近似目标的含义：不得把近似值写成 `target_context` 中要求
   精确匹配的数值。近似工况及其电极、全电池归属可写在同一 `evidence_claim`

   “低成本”等定性目标须区分文献提出的成本动机与已量化的价格优势；未提供价格数据

   定性或断言型要求（如“无集流体/壳体腐蚀被观测到”“无析钠/无枝晶”“提高首圈库仑效率”
   “该添加剂抑制产气”）不得写成 `mechanism_keyword` 关键词表——关键词命中分不清
   “发生腐蚀”与“未发生腐蚀”。改用 `kind: "evidence_claim"`：在 `claim` 里用一句
   用户原话写出对单个候选须成立的断言，在 `claim_verdicts` 里**逐候选**给出判定。
   语义判断（这段原文是否为该候选建立或推翻该断言）由你负责；程序只做两件可机械
   核验的事：判定须指向本次请求的候选，`quote` 须在该候选证据正文中逐字存在。
   因此措辞、否定、同义称呼的变化都不影响判定，你只需如实读原文：
   - `supported`：有原文明确为该候选建立断言，附 `chunk_id` 与逐字 `quote`；
   - `refuted`：有原文明确反驳（如原文说“会持续腐蚀铝箔”），附 `chunk_id` 与逐字 `quote`；
   - `not_found`：检索到的证据未直接提及，如实填写，由补证机制驱动下一轮检索。
   背景介绍、他人体系的结果、无实验支撑的预测都不算 `supported`。例如：
   ```json
   {
     "constraint_id": "no-corrosion",
     "description": "no current-collector or case corrosion observed",
     "kind": "evidence_claim",
     "claim": "该候选电解液不腐蚀铝箔或钢壳",
     "claim_verdicts": [
       {
         "candidate_id": "candidate-1",
         "verdict": "refuted",
         "chunk_id": "fan2024::sec3",
         "quote": "the single NaFSI system can continuously corrode aluminum foil and stainless steel sheets",
         "basis": "原文明确说明单盐 NaFSI 会持续腐蚀铝箔与不锈钢，与该断言相反。"
       }
     ],
     "can_replan": true,
     "search_hint": "find corrosion test evidence for the candidate electrolyte"
   }
   ```
   `evidence_claim` 不得把 `required_evidence_scope` 设为 `component` 或 `background`：
   断言必须由候选自身绑定的证据支持，不能借用别篇论文或背景段落的措辞。
   给出 `supported` 前，逐句核对引文是否真正支持所写断言。引文必须从指定
   `chunk_id` 返回的原文复制，不能把题名、摘要或另一块文字放在该块的标识下。
   配方、测试条件和性能必须对应同一候选；一种优点不能替代另一项目标的证据。
   成本动机与价格比较分别表述，安全性或无氟组成不能自行推导出成本优势。
   `basis` 说明原句与断言的推理关系，不得以重复断言代替理由。程序核验引文
   存在及归属，不代替科学含义判断；证据未支持完整断言时应补证或保留 `not_found`。
   `criteria`/`target_conditions` 仅用于兼容旧调用方；新设计任务必须优先使用
   `constraint_records`，避免 evaluator 再从自由文本猜测硬约束。

   `required_evidence_kinds` 描述的是**支持记录本身的语义角色**，不是实验条件元数据。
   数值性能约束通常只要求 `property`；温度、电极、循环数等共同实例化条件应由该
   observation 的 `condition_scope` 和 `joint_context_requirements` 表达。除非硬约束本身
   确实要求一条独立的 condition 记录，否则不要把同一数值约束写成
   `required_evidence_kinds=["property", "condition"]`，否则会把“带条件上下文的性能观测”
   错当成缺少第二种证据角色。

   当两个及以上硬约束必须在**同一个目标实验上下文**中同时成立时，还必须显式写
   `joint_context_requirements`。分别在多个倍率测试的要求，按倍率分别建立条件组，
   每组的 `target_context.rate` 只填一个倍率。不能把 `0.5 C and 1 C` 当成一次测试的倍率。
   同一论文的不同盐浓度或溶剂比例必须分别对应其性能段，不能因来自同篇论文就互换结果。
   `target_context.cell_configuration` 使用条件检查器的外形名称 `pouch` 或 `coin`，
   不拼成 `pouch full cell` 这样的新标签。全电池要求另用 cell_configuration 检查条件
   和明确的正负极对验证；外形名称不能代替电极与全电池要求。
   它描述的是 evidence composition obligation，不要求所有
   支持证据拥有相同 `experiment_id`。`constraint_ids` 只能引用本次 `constraint_records`；
   `context_fields` 只列对联合决策真正相关的字段；`target_context` 只填写用户明确给出的
   目标条件，未知字段保持未知，禁止为了让 join 成立而补默认值。例如：
   ```json
   {
     "joint_context_requirements": [
       {
         "group_id": "low-temp-high-voltage",
         "constraint_ids": ["retention", "voltage"],
         "context_fields": ["temperature_c", "electrode"],
         "target_context": {"temperature_c": -20.0, "electrode": "hard carbon"},
         "can_replan": true,
         "search_hint": "find evidence satisfying both hard constraints at the target operating context"
       }
     ]
   }
   ```
   只有约束确实需要共同实例化时才声明 joint group；互不相关的硬约束不要强行合组。
   原文条件检查器分别识别 `electrode` 与 `cell_configuration`。涉及电池形式的用户要求
   使用独立的 cell_configuration 条件；只有相关观测明确提供该字段时，才作联合检查。
2. 检查用户输入与已有 ledger；存在组分、机理或替代体系缺口时，选择相应检索能力；
3. 如证据不足，再做有界补充检索：
   - 区分“已有候选缺少一段证据”和“已有候选并不适合目标”。先检查最相关论文；
     若当前候选仍不能满足目标，按缺口与完整目标检索其他候选，不反复只查原来的
     盐、溶剂或论文。新证据支持新的组成时重新组装候选，再用原任务的全部条件
     筛选。不能把不同候选的成本、工况或性能拼成一个通过的候选。
   - 尚未定位候选论文时，用 `search_literature_chunks` 做 1–2 次聚焦补充（`top_k=10`）；
   - 若返回结果已经给出明确 `paper_id`，且该论文与目标组分/机理直接相关但缺少显式配方或目标工况证据，必须对最相关的 1 篇论文调用一次 `search_paper_chunks(paper_id=..., query=..., top_k=8)`；`query` 用 4–8 个英文技术词描述缺失事实，不含作者名。将结果追加到 `evidence_chunks`，不得跨论文拼接配方与性能。
   - 对 **named-study / named-candidate** 设计任务，在进入 `query_formulation_space` 或
     `screen_formulations` 前，必须先取得同一论文中可追溯的配方/组成证据：至少有一条
     `evidence_kind="formulation"` 的记录能支持候选的盐、溶剂或添加剂组成。只有性能、温度、
     机理 chunk 不能建立候选配方归属；若当前只找到性能证据，应继续检索 formulation /
     composition 段落，而不是手工构造一个 `formulation_evidence_ids=[]` 的候选进入筛选。
4. 用户没有提供可评估候选时，调用 `query_formulation_space`，把目标转成：
   `{"request":{"task_type":"design","target_conditions":[...],"preferred_salts":[...],"preferred_solvents":[...],"preferred_additives":[...],"excluded_components":[...],"evidence_chunks": evidence_chunks,"max_candidates":3}}`；其中 `evidence_chunks` 必须传入前面检索实际返回、与目标最相关的最多 12 个 chunk，不得只传组分偏好而丢失文献上下文。工具会优先从这些同论文原文块组装候选，再使用 KG fallback；保留工具原样返回的 `candidates`。
   如果候选 evidence 只有 `chunk_id` 而 `text/excerpt` 为空，先调用
   `enrich_formulation_evidence({"request":{"candidates": candidates}})`，并用返回候选
   替换原列表；证据已有原文时不得为形式完整重复调用。enrichment 只补齐原文和元数据，
   必须保留原 evidence 的 `paper_id`、`evidence_kind` 和 `chunk_id`。
5. 若任务涉及离子电导率、温度下的传输性质或需要在多个 NaPF6–EC/EMC/PC 候选之间增加一个轻量定量参考，可在筛选前调用 `predict_formulation_conductivity`。只有以下两种情况允许数值预测：候选已有明确的 NaPF6/EC/EMC/PC 摩尔组成，或调用参数中的 `composition_inputs[candidate_id]` 显式给出 `component_mmol`、`molar_ratios` 或 `x_NaSalt/x_EC/x_PC`。现有 `solvent_ratios` 没有保存 v/v、w/w 或 molar 基准，因此**不得**仅凭“1 M + 1:1”之类字段推导模型输入。含其他盐、其他溶剂或添加剂的候选按域外处理；组成不足时保留 `insufficient_composition`，继续依赖文献/KG 证据。`model_predictions` 与 literature evidence 必须分开：模型预测可以辅助候选比较和后续实验优先级，但不能单独把实验事实型硬约束判为满足。
6. 只有需要形成配方推荐或明确 hold 时才调用 `screen_formulations`：
   传入当前候选和完整的结构化 `constraint_records`。旧文本字段用于兼容历史输入，
   新设计任务不能用它们替代结构化条件。
   每项 `claim_verdicts` 只判定本次 `candidates` 中实际提交的候选。候选集合变更时，
   同步更新各断言的候选判定，保持原任务的全部条件。工具返回参数错误后，修复
   指出的字段并重新提交完整请求，不得删去 `constraint_records` 或联合条件来消除报错。
    倍率与循环次数是两种不同测试，分别建立约束：指定 1 C 测试使用
    `{"kind":"c_rate","operator":"==","value":1,"unit":"C"}`；
    100 次循环使用 `{"kind":"minimum_cycles","value":100,"unit":"cycles"}`。
    指定 2.0–4.0 V 测试使用
    `{"kind":"voltage_window","operator":"==","value":[2.0,4.0],"unit":"V"}`。
    若任务要求 0.5 C 和 1 C，各自建立条件。
    双盐配方同时保存 `salts` 与 `salt_concentrations_mol_l`，分别记录各盐浓度；
    `concentration_mol_l` 表示总盐浓度，不得将它归给某一个盐。
    `solvent_ratio_basis` 按原文填写 `mass`、`volume` 或 `molar`；原文未说明时填
    `unknown`。不得把质量比例当成体积比例，或把溶剂比例直接当成包括盐的摩尔组成。
   若本任务已声明 `joint_context_requirements`，每次首次筛选和补证后的重新筛选都必须携带
   同一份 joint-context 合同；除非用户明确修改任务目标，否则不得在 re-screen 时删除、
   放宽 `context_fields` 或改写 `target_context`。runtime 会在字段被意外省略时保留上一版
   显式合同，但 Agent 仍应主动原样传递。
   保留工具原样返回的 `screening_results`、其中的 `criteria_evaluations` 与 `gaps`，
   不得手写分数、validations 或 scores。任何 `failed`、`insufficient_evidence` 或
   `unsupported` 判定都不得在报告中表述为性能已验证。
7. 旧调用方需要动作列表时，可调用 `optimize_formulations`：
   `{"candidates": candidates,"screening_results": screening_results,"request":{"task_type":"design","objectives":[目标性能...],"constraints":[用户硬约束...]}}`。
   不得同时传入 `validations` 或 `scores`。该兼容工具只翻译筛选后已经产生的
   `DecisionState`，不会再按 score 独立裁决；若 proposal 为
   `retrieve_more_evidence`，先执行对应的补充检索和重新筛选，再进入报告。
8. `DecisionState` 已达到 `recommend` 或 `hold` 后，必须**立即**调用 `synthesize_design_report`
   生成完整报告，并传入同一份原始 `screening_results`：
   `{"request":{"task_type":"design","question":用户问题,"evidence_chunks": evidence_chunks,"candidates": candidates,"screening_results": screening_results}}`。
   为提升 `claim_supported_ratio`，请在 `request.claims` 中提交**所有**被 `evidence_chunks` 直接支持的事实声明（`claim_type="fact"`），每条包含 `text`、对应 `chunk_id` 和唯一逐字原文引文 `evidence_quote`（必须从该 chunk 的 `content` 中逐字截取，且只出现一次）。**禁止为凑数量编造 claim**；若当前证据能直接支持的 claim 不足 2 条，应优先通过 `search_literature_chunks` 或 `search_paper_chunks` 补充检索，最多尝试 2 轮；若仍无法找到更多直接支持，则在报告中明确标注“证据不足”，并只提交已被验证的 claim。报告将渲染“已校验事实”小节，避免裁判从自由文本中抽取不被检索上下文支持的论断。
   报告要让使用者能安排下一步工作。用简明中文分别提交配方组成、文献的测试条件与数值、同条件基准配方的结果，并保留逐字引文。比例需说明质量比或体积比；浓度、添加剂用量不得省略或猜测。文献筛选不能写成新配方已由本智能体实验验证。
   当目标是某项性能时，报告必须包含已检索到的该项性能结果，不能只列出温度、
   电极和电压范围等测试设置。不同盐浓度、溶剂比例和添加剂分支的结果分别绑定到
   其配方。不得借用另一分支较好的结果；保留同一分支完整组成与性能已明确的候选，
   不必强求选取数值最高但组成仍缺失的分支。
   `next_steps` 按本次缺口列出具体核查或实验，包括要比较的配方、温度、倍率、电池类型和测量项目；这些是验证计划，不是已取得的结果。即使为 `hold`，也要展示已取得的候选资料、文献结果和暂缓原因，不得只写状态或检索流程。
   对没有数值判据的选材目标，`next_steps` 也要交代其验证状态。例如成本目标
   需要区分文献的成本动机与实际价格比较，不能因筛选通过就宣称全部目标已验证。
   性能类 `claims` 应优先包含与当前候选直接相连的实验结果，少选一般背景介绍。
   **关键纪律**：一旦 `screen_formulations` 返回 `hold` 或 `recommend`，**不得**再尝试重新构建候选、重新检索或输出自由文本；下一动作必须是 `synthesize_design_report`。若状态为 `search`，最多只做一轮补充检索 + 重新筛选，然后必须进入报告。
9. 直接输出报告全文，不得改写或截断。

## 退出纪律

- 不要求无条件调用所有工具；根据用户已有候选和结构化 evidence gaps 选择能力。
- `synthesize_design_report` 是终端编译能力。调用前必须已有终态 `DecisionState`；
  `search` 状态必须先按缺口补证或换候选，不能用固定工具次数代替状态判断。
- `recommend` 只推荐 approved candidates；`hold` 展示已检索的候选资料与文献结果，说明缺口和验证计划，不推荐或排序候选。

## 候选方案纪律

- 候选配方必须来自 KG 结构化证据或文献 chunk；
- 对于"建议组合"（无完整配方直接实验数据），summary 只写组分和证据来源，不写性能声明；
- 性能/效果声明只能绑定到直接支持该声明的 chunk_id；
- 禁止在"证据摘要"里写入未被任何 chunk 直接支持的推断句；无来源支撑的直接删除；
- **直接回答（direct_answer）只给出候选方案标识和最精简组成**，不要包含"已在某温度验证"、"性能最优"、"最有效"等需要跨证据推断的断言；
- 推荐完整配方必须有原文明确的钠盐浓度。若浓度未知，列为待补资料，不得填入
  “参考基准配方”的浓度并作为已有文献验证的配方推荐。

## 推荐/排序纪律

- 排序理由必须逐条绑定到具体 chunk_id，禁止写"C1/C3/C4 无法满足需求"、"某候选明显优于其他"等无直接对比证据的绝对化断言；
- 无直接对比证据时，只陈述各候选的组分、证据来源与评分，不给出相对优劣结论；
- 对"建议组合"的推荐，只能说明其组分和所依据的证据，不得把多篇证据的性能迁移到该组合上。

## 证据摘要纪律

- 配方段落若讨论多种浓度、多个溶剂比例或不同研究，先定位到单一配方的原文。
  不得把某段的浓度、另一配方的溶剂比例和第三个体系的添加剂拼成候选。
  原文工具返回中的数值、温度符号、配方标识和 chunk_id 应原样沿用，
  不得手工改写成另一温度或用整篇论文的共同身份代替相同测试条件。
- 每条 bullet 必须附带 `[chunk_id]`；
- 禁止输出以"【推断】"开头的句子；
- 禁止把多篇证据的性能迁移到某个候选配方上。

## 引用纪律

- 使用 `[chunk_id]` 格式；
- 禁止引用模型参数知识里的文献；
- 单篇报道就写"某文献报道/某体系显示"，不得升格为普适结论。

## KG 质量反馈

检索或分析过程中，若发现以下可疑情况，**必须**调用 `flag_suspicious_kg_item` 记录，供后续离线人工审查与 KG 矫正；不阻塞当前设计流程。

- **实体标签错误**：如 `ionic conductivity` 被标为 `Additive`，`NaPF6` 被标为 `Solvent`；
- **关系方向/语义错误**：如 `SEI DECOMPOSITION::FORMS::FEC`、明显违背化学常识的关系；
- **属性单位或数值异常**：如电导率 `100 mS/cm` 与上下文矛盾、温度单位混用；
- **同名异义**：如 `TMP` 同时指 `trimethyl phosphate` 与 `2,4,6-trimethylpyridine` 而未区分；
- **证据与 KG 矛盾**：chunk 中的明确结论与 KG 检索结果冲突。

记录时尽量提供：item_type（`entity`/`relation`/`property`）、具体名称/ID、问题描述、触发工具、证据 chunk_id。

## 知识沉淀

设计流程全部结束后，调用 `reflect_now` 进行知识反思和 Wiki 沉淀，
将本次设计的关键结论、发现的知识缺口、改进的检索关键词记录到 LLM Wiki，
供下次相似问题时直接检索复用，减少重复检索成本。

additional_kwargs.reasoning_content:
Let me plan the task. User: design an evidence-acquisition workflow to select and compare additive branches for NFM||hard-carbon sodium-ion pouch cell at -20 °C and 1 C (900 mA).

Interpretation: "-20 C" here — "at -20 C and 1 C (900 mA)". The "-20 C" appears right after "at" modifying... Actually "a pouch cell at -20 C" would be temperature. And "and 1 C (900 mA)" is the rate. So -20 °C temperature and 1 C rate = 900 mA. So current 900 mA implies 1 C capacity ~900 mAh. Pouch cell. NFM = Na Fe Mn oxide (NaFeMnO2 / NFM cathode), hard carbon anode.

So constraints: temperature -20 °C, c_rate 1 C, cell_configuration pouch, electrode_material NFM cathode + hard carbon anode, and the specific current 900 mA.

Additive branches: we need to select and compare additive branches (e.g., FEC, VC, etc.) for low-temperature performance.

Let me set up todos and start retrieval.

To verify the practical applicability of CIE, we assembled a 1.2 Ah (163 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ) pouch cell with O3-type NFM positive electrode and HC negative electrode (Fig. 6a). Figure 6b shows the cycling performance of the pouch cell at different temperatures. At 25 °C, the pouch cell provides a capacity of 1.18 Ah. As the temperature decreases, we verify the possibility of its operation at low temperatures, at -50 °C, the pouch cell still provides a capacity of 0.79 Ah (107 Wh kg $^{-1}$ ), demonstrating a significantly better low-temperature adaptability than that of conventional electrolytes. Moreover, even at -50 °C, the charge/discharge curve maintains a stable voltage plateau (Fig. 6c). Figure 6d shows the cycling performance of the pouch cell at -20 °C with 94.1% capacity retention after 300 cycles. In addition, in order to visually verify the practical application potential, the LED lights are continuously powered at a low temperature of -50 °C. The fully-charged state pouch cells keep the LED lights working for more than 10 hours (Fig. 6e). This demonstration confirms that the CIE has good prospects for practical applications, especially at low temperatures. We further compare our results with some previously reported low-temperature sodium-ion pouch cells (Fig. 6f, Table S6) $^{26,52-58}$ , and our work is comparable to most of the advanced reported works, which fully proves that the CIE developed by us has important application value for SIBs in cold environments. More detailed pouch cell parameters are shown in Table S7.

Conclusions
In summary, we have successfully synthesized a multifunctional SA electrolyte additive for pouch NFM/HC sodium-ion batteries, enabling stable electrochemical performance across a wide operating temperature range ( $-20$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ ). The multifunctional role of the SA-containing electrolyte can be attributed to a combination of synergistic effects, including the regulation of $Na^{+}$ solvation structure to accelerate interfacial reaction kinetics and enhance electrochemical stability at low temperatures, the scavenging residual water to preserve the structural stability of the cathode and suppress excessive gas evolution, thereby enhancing high-temperature performance, and the preferential redox decomposition of SA on the anode surface to form a high-quality interfacial film that protects the electrode and reduces interfacial resistance. Collectively, this work provides new insights into the rational design and optimization of electrolyte additives for practical all-climate pouch SIBs and other advanced energy storage systems.

The influence of incorporating various concentrations of NaTFPB on the NFM111 cathode was investigated through electrochemical measurements employing NFM111||Na half-cells. The rate capabilities of the half-cells with different electrolytes are depicted in Fig. 2a. Notably, the electrolyte containing 1.0 wt% NaTFPB exhibits superior rate performance, especially at high currents, due to its low interfacial resistance compared to the electrolytes with other concentrations. Even returned to 0.5 C, the discharged capacity of the electrolyte containing 1.0 wt% NaTFPB remains notably higher than that of the other electrolytes, recovering to 133.36 mAh g $^{-1}$ . Moreover, cyclic stability tests of the different electrolytes were conducted at a current density of 1.0 C (Fig. 2b). The results reveal that the 1.0 wt% NaTFPB electrolyte delivers a capacity retention of 70 % after 500 cycles at a current density of 1.0 C, significantly outperforming the Base electrolyte and other additive concentrations. Consequently, the concentration of NaTFPB additives was standardized to 1.0 wt%. Corresponding charge–discharge curves are presented in Fig. 2c-e. This enhancement was attributed to the additional active Na $^{+}$ provided by the NaTFPB additive, which increased the first-cycle discharge specific capacity. Conclusion
In this work, TDFP is firstly developed to design functional electrolytes and successfully achieve enhanced temperature performance of pouch NFM/HC cells. Compared to the NaDFP-containing electrolyte, the TDFP-containing electrolyte owns superior physical properties, and also can form much tougher SEI/CEI than that of TMSP. What's more, TDFP own a unique “formation-repair” film-formation behavior which induced rich-NaF SEI/CEI before/during charging. additional_kwargs.reasoning_content:
0017_Fan 2026: TDFP additive branch (1% mass ratio in 0.8 M NaPF6 EC:EMC 3:7), NFM/HC pouch; low-T: TDFP 86% discharge capacity retention at -30 °C; low temperature cycling at -10 °C. Not -20 °C explicitly, but -30 °C retention. No -20 °C number.

OK. Now build the final candidate set. I'll include 5 branches (each from a distinct paper, with formulation):
1. c-sa: 1 M NaPF6 / EC:EMC 3:7 (mass) / 1 wt% SA — 0045_Lu 2025 → -20 °C 1C 638.2 mAh.
2. c-nadfp: 0.8 M NaPF6 / EC:EMC 3:7 / 1.0 wt% NaDFP — 0002_Cai 2024 → -20 °C 1C 798 mAh.
3. c-tmsbs: 1 M NaPF6 / EC:EMC 3:7 (mass) / 1 wt% TMSBS — 0031_Li 2025 → no -20 °C (has -30 °C ≤0.5C, -10 °C 1C cycling).
4. c-natfpb: 1.0 M NaPF6 / EC:DMC 1:1 (mass) + 5.0% FEC / 1.0 wt% NaTFPB — 0024_Hu 2025 → -20 °C 0.5C at 4.1 V, not 1C.
5. c-tdfp: 0.8 M NaPF6 / EC:EMC 3:7 / 1 wt% TDFP — 0017_Fan 2026 → -30 °C 86% retention; -10 °C cycling.

Hmm, and NB (NaDFP+TMSB) from 0156 — additive amounts unknown. And 0031's TMSBS. I think 5 is enough; but should I include the NB dual-additive branch since it's an additive branch with -30 °C 1C data in NFM/HC pouch (729/697 mAh)? Including it makes 6 candidates. The complication: additive amount unknown (1:1.5 ratio, mass fraction not stated) → composition incomplete → I'd include it as a candidate with a gap. I think including NB is valuable for the "compare additive branches" ask since it explicitly compares two additive branches in one paper (NP vs NB). But then symmetric treatment would require NP too...

Decision: include 6 candidates: SA, NaDFP, TDFP, TMSBS, NaTFPB, and NB (NaDFP+TMSB). Hmm, that's a lot but fine. Actually, wait: 0156's NB additive amounts unknown; the -20 °C numeric absent. Including it adds noise. Let me instead include 5 with complete compositions (SA, NaDFP, TDFP, TMSBS, NaTFPB) and mention 0156 NB/NP as a cross-check branch in the report narrative... But the report's claims must be chunk-bound; I can add a claim about 0156's -30 °C 1C result of NB/NP as a fact claim (it's directly supported). But if a branch with promising low-T data (NB "-30 °C 1C 697 mAh", "more suitable for low-temperature application") is excluded from candidates without reason, that's a weak selection. Hmm — reason: additive mass fraction not reported in the retrieved text (composition incomplete) and no -20 °C numeric. That is a legitimate documented exclusion. But the screening tool would show that gap nicely.

I'll include it as the 6th candidate with additive_amounts giving the ratio and note gap. Actually careful: adding candidates that fail on composition could trigger "search" state and force another retrieval round. The runtime may return hold/search. That's acceptable — I'm prepared for one re-search round. But hold reduces usefulness... Let's think about which outcome is right.

Hard constraints: exact -20 °C and 1 C, pouch, NFM||HC, additive amount explicit, concentration explicit. 
- c-sa: temp -20 (yes), rate 1C (yes), pouch yes, electrodes yes, additive 1 wt% yes, conc 1 M yes → passes all.
- c-nadfp: -20 yes, 1C yes, pouch yes, HC/NFM yes, additive 1 wt% yes, conc 0.8 M yes → passes.
- c-tdfp: -30 °C only, -10 °C cycling; -20 °C? The text mentions tests "at low temperature" with Fig 4a rate, and "-30 °C 86% retention". No -20 °C. → fails temp.
- c-tmsbs: fails temp.
- c-natfpb: -20 °C at 0.5 C not 1 C → fails rate (though current? the 4.1 V/0.5C). fails.
- c-nb: -20 °C not quantified → fails temp claim; composition incomplete → fails field.

So 2 of 6 pass → DecisionState likely "recommend" with the 2 approved. Good — and the comparison is meaningful.

I'll go with 6 candidates. Hmm, the NB one: let me just include it; it demonstrates the comparison requirement and gives a documented gap.

Actually, to be careful about the additivity: the NB evidence chunk (0156 sec8::child3) — verdict for -20 °C/1C claim = not_found. But it has -30 °C 1C. Fine.

Wait — for the -20 °C & 1 C claim, what about TDFP? Its chunk says TDFP maintained 86% discharge capacity retention at -30 °C. For 1 C? Unclear. not_found.

evidence_chunks.chunk_id: 0045_Lu 等 - 2025 - All-climate carbonate electrolyte with 2-sulfobenzoic anhydride additive leads the way to high-perfo::sec4::child0
evidence_chunks.content:
Sodium hexafluorophosphate (NaPF $_6$ ), ethylene carbonate (EC), and methyl ethyl carbonate (EMC) were supplied by Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co., Ltd. A baseline electrolyte was prepared by dissolving NaPF $_6$ (1 mol/L) into a mixed solvent of EC and EMC (weight ratio 3:7). To formulate a functional electrolyte, 1 wt% 2-Sulfobenzoic anhydride (SA) was added to the baseline system. The NFM cathode and hard carbon (HC) anode active materials were procured from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co., Ltd. and Kuraray Co., Ltd., respectively. The NFM cathode slurry consisted of 94.5 wt% NFM, 1.8 wt% PVDF, 1 wt% carbon nanotubes (CNT), 2.5 wt% Super P, and 0.2 wt% maleic acid dispersed in $N$ -methylpyrrolidone (NMP), and was cast onto aluminum foil. The HC anode was composed of 95 wt% HC,

![](images/8bfcb630e9de984c98fbfc69f2dd0cb440e9bd8293373fa0ec9806e9fb6d55de.jpg)  
Fig. 1. 2-Sulfobenzoic anhydride (SA) is introduced as electrolyte additive to enhance the electrochemical performance of pouch SIBs.

1.5 wt% carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), 2 wt% styrene-butadiene rubber (SBR), and 1.5 wt% Super P. A Celgard 2700 membrane (Xingyuan Materials Co., Ltd.) was employed as the separator. The areal mass loadings of the cathode and anode were 33.0 and 20.1 mg/cm $^{2}$ , respectively, with a negative-to-positive (N/P) capacity ratio of 1.1 (based on theoretical capacity calculation).

evidence_chunks.chunk_id: 0045_Lu 等 - 2025 - All-climate carbonate electrolyte with 2-sulfobenzoic anhydride additive leads the way to high-perfo::sec7::child10
evidence_chunks.content: Under more extreme conditions, discharge tests at $-20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ (Fig. 4a) revealed that cells with SA-based electrolyte delivered discharge capacities of 758.6, 702.2 and $638.2\mathrm{mAh}$ at $0.2\mathrm{C}$ , $0.5\mathrm{C}$ , and $1\mathrm{C}$ ( $1\mathrm{C} = 900\mathrm{mA}$ ), respectively, outperforming those with the baseline electrolyte, which exhibited 706.3, 636.8 and $563.6\mathrm{mAh}$ . These results confirm that SA facilitates higher energy density and improved capacity retention at low temperatures, rendering it well-suited for emergency storage applications in cold environments. In addition, the rate capability of sodium-ion batteries at ambient temperature is critical for practical deployment. High-rate performance enables rapid charge/discharge cycles, a requirement for power-intensive applications such as electric vehicles and portable electronics [27a,28]. As shown in Fig. 4d, the SA containing system exhibited superior rate capacity, indicating enhanced commercial viability. Long-term cycling at 1C was also evaluated at room temperature (Figs. 4c and S7). During extended cycling, the baseline electrolyte showed faster polarization growth, whereas the SA-based system demonstrated superior capacity retention and enhanced coulombic efficiency. These characteristics contribute to reduced energy losses and extended battery lifespan, which are advantageous for grid-scale and commercial energy storage [29].

evidence_chunks.chunk_id: 0045_Lu 等 - 2025 - All-climate carbonate electrolyte with 2-sulfobenzoic anhydride additive leads the way to high-perfo::sec2::child0
evidence_chunks.content: A multifunctional additive, 2-sulfobenzoic anhydride (SA), was synthesized from the readily available saccharin, then 1 % SA was added into carbonate-based electrolytes to enhance the performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) employing $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM) cathodes and hard carbon (HC) anodes across a wide temperature range from $-20\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . The commercial pouch cells delivered a capacity retention of 90.52 % after 300 cycles at room temperature and 92.28 % after 300 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ . Low-temperature rate performance at $-20\ ^{\circ}C$ and cycling at $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ further demonstrated the excellent adaptability of SA-containing electrolytes under sub-zero temperature. Moreover, under high-voltage operation at 4.0 V, the SA-containing electrolyte effectively suppressed capacity fading, resulting in an 11.44 % improvement in capacity retention. Compared to conventional commercial electrolytes, this electrolyte enables interfacial optimization by suppressing excessive growth of cathode and anode interphases, also it eliminates detrimental electrolyte components, tune the solvation structure and promote interfacial reaction kinetics. In situ gas analysis conducted during cycling at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ revealed that SA significantly inhibits gas-evolving side reactions, thereby ensuring the safety of SIBs.
